title: Your Eyes Read Words You Swear Were Blank, Yet One 300-Millisecond Wave Sparks Awareness
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Stanislas Dehaene (2006): Global Neuronal Workspace — The 300-Millisecond 'Brain-Wide Ignition' That Turns Sight Into Consciousness!, grounded in Stanislas Dehaene, Jean-Pierre Changeux, Lionel Naccache, Jérôme Sackur et al. (2006) (Trends in Cognitive Sciences). Empirical findings show that for centuries, consciousness — how silent electromagnetic tissue turns light on your retina into 'I SEE THAT WORD!' — was taboo in hard neuroscience, dismissed as an untestable mystery until Stanislas Dehaene, Jean-Pierre Changeux, and Lionel Naccache built a clean laboratory switch (*May 2006, Trends in Cognitive Sciences, SRC1; Neuron 2011, SRC2*).

At the circuit level, this episode examines how primary visual cortex, parietal cortex, prefrontal cortex coordinate behavioral and neural responses, alongside evidence that how do you study pure consciousness scientifically? Hold the physical word on the screen 100% constant (say, a 43-millisecond flash of the word LION), and dial a visual mask milliseconds closer or further (Del Cul, Baillet & Dehaene 2007, SRC3) so on half the trials you swear the screen was blank, and on the other half the word pops vividly into awareness.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Stanislas Dehaene, Jean-Pierre Changeux, Lionel Naccache, Jérôme Sackur et al. (2006). Conscious, preconscious, and subliminal processing: a testable taxonomy. Trends in Cognitive Sciences. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.tics.2006.03.007
- George A. Mashour, Pieter Roelfsema, Jean-Pierre Changeux, Stanislas Dehaene (2020). Conscious Processing and the Global Neuronal Workspace Hypothesis. Neuron. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2020.01.026
- Antoine Del Cul, Sylvain Baillet, Stanislas Dehaene (2007). Brain Dynamics Underlying the Nonlinear Threshold for Access to Consciousness. PLoS Biology. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0050260
